final_answer: DURING THE DAY, SUNLIGHT TRAVELS THROUGH A SHORTER PATH IN THE ATMOSPHERE. BLUE LIGHT (SHORTER WAVELENGTH) IS SCATTERED MORE BY MOLECULES (RAYLEIGH SCATTERING) THAN RED LIGHT (LONGER WAVELENGTH). THIS SCATTERED BLUE LIGHT FILLING THE SKY MAKES IT APPEAR BLUE. AT SUNSET, SUNLIGHT TRAVELS THROUGH A LONGER PATH, SCATTERING MOST BLUE LIGHT AWAY. LESS SCATTERED RED/ORANGE LIGHT DOMINATES, MAKING THE SKY RED. RAYLEIGH SCATTERING (INTENSITY ∝ 1/λ⁴) EXPLAINS WHY SHORTER WAVELENGTHS SCATTER STRONGER, BUT LONGER PATHS REDUCE BLUE VISIBILITY.
